briefs.name: Quote Board, Lit Figures
briefs.hypothesis: Quote Board, Posted lost ground for one reason all eight lenses named: the board below the greeting has no light of its own, and it reads as three boxed widgets. Its type system is already the best in the field (first for type, interaction 7.9) and its head device is the app's page-head standard. Three changes should take it past the 7.9 tie at the top. First, a law the line can own: a figure that COUNTS is printed in its section's ink, and a figure that is LIVE is lit phosphor with the original tube's halo. Second, the tube becomes a quote screen that draws real data. Third, the boxes come off so the board reads as typeset columns. That brings the original's light back exactly where the eye should land, keeps grounded colour everywhere else, and gives the line a signature no other design has: lit numerals rather than lit wires or rails.
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-quote-cross (palettes/x14a-quote-cross.json, variants/x14a-quote-cross/). Keep its six-rule header, the three type voices (Archivo condensed display, Archivo text, Plex Mono data), the type steps (--t-legend to --t-mega), the quote head on every page (condensed title, figure in section ink, stacked unit over change), the slate materials and the one-row bar. Add a new layer, 'LIT FIGURES', at the foot of sheet.css, and rewrite rule 6 in the header as: 'A figure that counts is ink; a figure that is live is light.'

THE LAW (sheet.css and every template). Add a utility class .fig-live: VT323 or Archivo 300 numerals in var(--screen), with the kit's E1 layered halo (text-shadow 0 0 1px var(--hot), 0 0 6px var(--halo-70), 0 0 18px var(--halo-35)) and E9 afterglow on arrival (the existing arrival flash, held to 2.4s so the 1.8s still catches it lit). On each page exactly one figure carries .fig-live: Home's next stop day numeral; Status's working count; Chat's newest-reply time; Plans' next day numeral; To do's NOW lamp, which is a lamp rather than a figure. Every other quote figure stays in its section ink at weight 300: steel-cyan --plans, wheat --todo, heather --ideas, clay --people.

HOME.
(a) Greeting plate (.welcome). New title, set on two lines: 'What should' / 'Vera *plan?*', with the question mark inside the lit run and E1 at full strength. Keep the box, the From row and the starters. Confine the green pool: set washGlow from 2.4 to 1.2 in the palette, and give .welcome overflow:clip with the ::before pool masked to the plate (mask-image: linear-gradient(#000 70%, transparent)), so nothing washes Lately added (skeptic).
(b) The tube on the right becomes a QUOTE SCREEN, drawing data in place of the stock Next up box. Top left: the NEXT UP inverse tag, then 'Oaks Park roller rink' in VT323 at 1.6rem, then 'Sun 4 Oct · 13:00' in VT323 at the dim strength. Top right: the quote itself, a VT323 '2' at about 5rem in the bright strength with full bloom, and 'DAYS' stacked under it. Across the tube's foot runs a four-week tick tape (see graft 2): a baseline from NOW to +4W, a tick at each plan's day labelled 4, 9, 17 and 24 in VT323, and the first tick bright with a lamp dot and halo, the others at 45%. 'All plans ›' sits at the tape's end. Keep the E12 case, power light and E13/E14 scanlines. The radar gives way here.
(c) Setup band (.alert.setup, .setup-track). Shrink the rings from 44px to 28px with a 1.5px var(--steel) stroke. The current step is a 10px amber lamp inside its ring, and no ring is outlined in amber. The figure '3' stays amber (setup is a caution), and 'Next: choose your own password →' stays. The band keeps a 44px hit height on its links.
(d) The board (.board, .tile). Take the boxes off. Drop each .tile's border, background and radius. Each column now stands under a 2px cap rule in its section ink (border-top: 2px solid var(--tile)) with a 1px var(--rule) hairline between columns. Set grid-auto-rows:min-content so no column keeps an empty tray, and put the feet on one shared baseline row. Head: label, dotted leader, figure on the label's baseline, with the legend's top line on the figure's cap height (system).
  - Coming up: the figure is '4' (all four plans, so it matches Plans) in steel-cyan, with the unit 'plans'. The register starts at plan 1. Its first row (.hop.is-next) carries the lit date: the day '4' sits on a 3.25rem tiny tube (ledger L026: green-black glass, a 1-in-3 raster, a lit top edge, the numeral in .fig-live VT323 at 2.4rem), with 'Next · in 2 days' in var(--lit) at the row's end. A 2px phosphor NOW tick stands at the row's left edge. Rows 2 to 4 keep Archivo 300 bone day numerals with the month and weekday stacked, Plex times in a fixed column, and 'in 7 days' right. Plan titles are NOT underlined at rest: the underline appears on :hover and :focus-visible only. That rule holds on every row title on every page.
  - To do: the figure '4' in BONE (var(--heading)) under the wheat cap, so the colour never sits beside amber 'was due' (skeptic, usability, system). The rows are square steel wells (border 1.5px var(--well-edge), never amber), title, who, then 'was due 5 days ago' in amber words with a 2px amber left edge. A NOW divider (the To do page's: a 6px breathing lamp, E20, 'NOW' in Plex legend and a hairline in var(--lit) at 40%) runs between the late and the undated. The foot reads '3 late →' in amber and 'All 4 →'.
  - Lately added: the figure '12' in heather. The first idea is set large as now. The rest is a register with the kind icon in its ink, the title in text 500 and who, all on one line.
(e) The household row, rebuilt as a TICKER TAPE so it no longer copies Settled's five boxed cells. It is one unboxed line under a 1px rule, like a trading tape: 'Wishes Maya 0 · Theo 0 | Memory — | Family 4 people | Status ● 6 working | Settings 3 to finish'. Each label is text 500 at --t-small in --label, each figure Archivo 300 at --t-lead in its owner's ink (shows pink, people clay, plans steel, amber for 'to finish'), and the separators are thin --rule pipes. Each segment is a link at least 44px tall. The Status segment now says '6 working', the Status page's own count, so the two figures agree (interaction, usability). On the phone the tape wraps to two lines and never scrolls the page.
(f) Phone (390px): the starters become one row that scrolls sideways inside the plate (overflow-x:auto, scroll-snap, a 16px gutter, no page scroll). The quote screen drops to its tag, title, '2 DAYS' and the tape, so the next plan sits above the fold. The setup band follows the board.

CHAT. Head: 'Vera 2' with the stacked legend 'replies' over 'last 27 Sep · 19:53', where the time is the page's .fig-live (no false 'today'). Family bubbles become matte slate (--bubble-them) with no steel top edge or glow. Vera's older lines are bone ink on --bubble glass with a 1px border at 22% green. Only her NEWEST line keeps the phosphor edge, the E8 top highlight and the E9 afterglow, at body size (17px/1.5), never headline size (system, type).

TO DO page (tasks.html). Drop the '#4' ids from the title column. Show only the date when no hour was set ('was due Sun 27 Sep'). Row titles go to Archivo text 500 at 1.0625rem at normal width, not condensed 600 (type). The checkboxes are steel squares. The head figure '4' is bone, '3 late' is an amber link, and the latched keys Open / Late 3 / Done / Cancelled / All stay. The unit legends are sentence-case sans at 0.8125rem ('open', '3 late'), not tracked mono caps, on every page (type).

STATUS. The head stays 'Status 6 working / 7 off', with '6' as the .fig-live. The spend tube keeps '$0.00' in VT323 and gains a DAY RANGE BAR under it (see graft 3): a straight scale on a square-root spacing marked 0, 0.25, 1.00 and 2.00 in VT323 dim, a lit needle tick at today's spend with a hot core and halo, a dashed ghost tick at the 30-day average '$0.04', and 'avg $0.04 · limit $2.00' printed under it, so $0.00 still reads as a place on a scale. The lamp banks keep their figures in owners' inks, with 'needs a look' as an amber figure.

PLANS. The list uses the same hop rows, with the next stop's day numeral in the L026 tiny tube as the page's one live figure. In the month view, the cells give plan names 14px text 500 and rows 20% taller (usability).

IDEAS and FORM. Ideas keeps its kind keys unfolded on desktop. The new-idea form drops the '+1' figure: its head is the condensed title 'New idea' with the legend 'pick one of 7 kinds' and no figure (usability).

SETTINGS. Field labels are sentence-case Archivo 500 at 13px (type). Section heads keep the label-leader-figure line ('General ····· 9 parts').

COLOUR CHECK. Green stays at or under about 55% of saturated pixels on every page. No hue is removed without a replacement: the amber taken off the To do figure and the checkboxes goes to bone and steel, and the wheat stays as the To do cap.
briefs.borrows:
OWN JUDGES' FIXES (x14a-quote-cross, crossing 14a), most cited first:
1. Give Coming up's cell its own phosphor, a lit next-day numeral or NOW tick. Asked by feedback, soul, style, system, interaction, type and usability (7 of 8). Met by the lit-figure law, the L026 tiny tube and the NOW tick on the first hop.
2. Take the boxes off the cells: a hairline with a 2px section cap, or open columns. Asked by style and system, with feedback's 'board of boxes'. Met by removing .tile's borders and fills under 2px caps.
3. Amber with one job: steel checkboxes and a bone To do figure. Asked by the skeptic and usability, with system's earlier 'To do needs a hue other than caution'.
4. Lighter setup rings: about 28px, a steel stroke, amber only on the lamp. Asked by style and the skeptic, and recorded in crossing lessons.
5. No underlines on plan titles at rest, and the green pool confined to its plate. Asked by the skeptic, and recorded in crossing lessons.
6. Reconcile Home's Status figure with the Status page: '6 working' on both. Asked by interaction and usability.
7. Chat: family lines matte, the phosphor edge on her newest line only, an honest legend. Asked by system, interaction and usability.
8. Type: drop the #ids and the false hours on To do, set row titles in sans 500 at normal width, set units in sentence-case sans. Asked by type.
9. Make the Home tube draw data. Asked by soul.
10. Drop the form's '+1'. Asked by usability.
11. Stop the household row copying Settled's cells. Asked by soul and recorded in crossing lessons.

FROM THE LEDGER: L026 'The date leaf as a tiny tube' (r4-rand-5 Zinc Garden, a gem; full entry in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/ledger.md). It is used ONCE a page, for the next stop's day numeral, so the board's one point of phosphor is a little lit screen echoing the Home tube with the kit's E13/E14 bloom and raster.

THE PHOSPHOR KIT, restored at the lit points only (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/phosphor_kit.md): E1 on the lit word and every .fig-live, E7 confined to the plate, E9 on arrival and on her newest line, E12-E14 on the quote screen and the tiny date tube, E20 on the NOW lamps.

WHAT IT KEEPS: the quote head on every page, the three type voices and steps, the latched To do keys, Ideas' kind keys, the Status lamp banks with lit counts, the setup strip, the slate, bone, steel and denim, and the arrival flash.
WHAT IT GIVES UP: the Home tube's radar (the 404 keeps E17/E18), the tile boxes and their fills, Settled's five-cell household strip, the '+1' form figure, the To do ids and false hours, and the amber outlines.
briefs.avoids: It answers the line's two biggest criticisms. Against 'the board has no phosphor of its own' and 'the light stays at the hero corner' (all lenses), each list now carries one lit live figure. Against 'a board of boxes / a generic dashboard' (style, system, feedback), the board becomes open typeset columns under section caps. It takes amber off the To do figure and the checkboxes (the skeptic: 'half the board reads as a warning'), shrinks the heavy amber rings, removes the at-rest underlines and the spilled green pool, ends the household row that copied Settled, reconciles '1 of 3 lit' with '6 working', and quiets Chat's green. It also heeds the crossing lessons. It does not copy a rail with a NOW lamp or a wire (convergence: on nearly every design, and Listing's long wire failed). It does not stretch a container to fill space (Trued's and Manual's mistake). It does not take a feature the tour already failed. It drops the shared title, and it names the replacement hue (bone, steel) for every amber it removes.
briefs.title: "What should Vera *plan?*" A new, untried title, set on two lines broken before 'Vera', with 'plan?' lit and the question mark inside the lit run. It frees this line from 'Give Vera something to plan.', which seven crosses shared and which the 14b instructions keep for Desk alone in heat a. It keeps what the judges favoured in both favourites: like 'Give Vera something to plan.' it names who hears you, and like 'What needs a plan?' it is a question that cannot be answered 'no'. Its short lit job word ends the line, directly above the quote screen whose figure answers it ('2 DAYS' to the next plan). It is a question the family answers by typing, so it works as the box's label, and 'plan' takes in weekends, reminders, ideas and wishes alike.

reading: The judges love this line's type. Its quote head (a condensed title, a figure in section ink, a stacked unit over a change line) was first or near first for type in every round, and type, system and interaction want it as the app's page-head standard. Taking the costume off (keycaps, the Alt footer) lifted it from 7.09 to 7.58 and made it the calmest glance in the field (interaction 7.9, usability 7.7). Three things sank it. First and loudest, the board below the greeting has no light of its own: seven of eight lenses asked for Coming up's next day numeral to be lit, and soul said the light stays in the hero corner. Second, it reads as boxed widgets: three equal cards plus Settled's household strip, called 'a generic dashboard' and a copied strip. Third, amber has too many jobs: amber-outlined checkboxes, a wheat-amber To do figure beside amber 'was due', and heavy 44px amber setup rings. Smaller faults: plan titles underlined at rest, the green pool spilling onto Lately added, Home's Status '1 of 3 lit' against the Status page's '6 working', Chat bubbles too green, the '+1' form figure, '#id' and false-hour clutter on To do, and condensed 600 row titles. The title was shared with six other crosses. To win, it should keep its type system and its scarcity rule, and turn that rule into a law the owner's 'bring back the phosphor' ask rewards: a figure that counts is ink, a figure that is live is lit with the original tube's halo. That puts one point of real phosphor in every section, open typeset columns in place of boxes, a tube that quotes real data, and a title of its own. It should avoid the field's convergent rails and wires so that its signature, the lit numeral, stays its own.
